buckets.name: Methods
buckets.speed_limit: None inherent; capability can move fast. The paper's claim is that this stock is not the bottleneck.
buckets.stock: Capabilities and methods — what the frontier can do on benchmarks and in the lab.

buckets.name: Products
buckets.speed_limit: Reliability, integration, evaluation and liability — the 50%→80% gap and the "last mile" of productisation.
buckets.stock: Reliable, integrated products built on those methods.

buckets.name: Early adoption
buckets.speed_limit: Human and organisational speed — training, procurement, trust, ROI measurement (electrification took decades).
buckets.stock: Individuals and firms using the products, at any depth.

buckets.name: Adaptation
buckets.speed_limit: Complementary innovation, regulation, safety brakes and the pace of institutional change.
buckets.stock: Workflows, institutions, labour markets and regulation reorganised around the technology.

buckets.name: Return arrow
buckets.speed_limit: Whether the deployment→training channel is open and how far it substitutes for external bottlenecks.
buckets.stock: Deployment feedback flowing back into invention — data, RL environments, continual learning.

crosswalk.note: Capability growth is the model layer's product; inference price at fixed capability ⇄ price-per-token pass-through; open-weights lag ⇄ open-vs-closed gap.
Compute growth and hardware perf-per-dollar feed the methods stock.
Productisation runs through serving, routing and agent infrastructure.
Uplift RCTs, pilot→production and app-layer margin net of inference measure the same valve.
BTOS, BBD, Ramp and the Anthropic Economic Index are adoption from both ends.
Productivity, wages, employment and consumer surplus.
Deployment/FDE services capture part of the surplus that adaptation creates.
Adaptation measured inside deployed products: regulated devices built on language models and paid robotaxi rides.
Expert data, RL environments and continual-learning infra are the deployment→invention channel; lab recoupment ⇄ capex-to-revenue.
Margin stacking, HHI, circular financing: surplus exiting the chain at semis and cloud. Interpretive spine: Teece, Nordhaus and Perez in docs/interpretation; Ding through the bottleneck list.
Inside the labs: agent work on the labs' own research and lab recoupment are deployment feeding back into invention.
Backlash, safety brakes and paused runs are adaptation acting back on the model layer.
The public text stock and other training inputs bound how fast the methods stock can grow.
Adaptation inside adopting organisations and sectors: regulated devices, state bills, call-centre uplift, reported executive impact.
Reliability, calibration and the gap between internal and external deployment decide what the model layer can productise.
Buyers spreading work across several labs is adoption breadth read from the model layer.
People adopting directly: consumer and worker use counted from the household side.
Consumer surplus is where most of the value goes if the capture thesis fails: the leak to labour and consumers.

answers: Who keeps it: Model / Frontier labs
indicators.name: Top-three share of tracked venture dollars
indicators.unpublished_reason: Identical to frontier_capital_concentration on the seed list since Q2 2025 (the top three raisers are the frontier_labs sub-layer), so a separate status would count one fact twice; it publishes when a non-frontier company enters the top three.

indicators.name: Median round size by sub-layer
indicators.unpublished_reason: Not meaningful on current coverage: one to four seed-list rounds per sub-layer-quarter, so a median restates the venture strip's total and count; it needs a round source with market coverage (aifunding.me is on the read-not-ingested list; PitchBook, Crunchbase and Dealroom are paid).

indicators.name: Venture flow's lead or lag against sub-layer revenue (quarters)
indicators.unpublished_reason: Two things are missing: revenue by sub-layer, which only the labs report and only as press-relayed run-rates, and enough quarters to cross-correlate against. The venture series starts in 2023 and eight quarters of both sides are needed before a lag is more than noise.

indicators.name: Stage mix of venture rounds by sub-layer
indicators.unpublished_reason: Not measurable from free structured data: Form D has no round or series field, and Epoch's rounds (labs only) name the stage inside a free-text label; a stage mix by sub-layer needs PitchBook, Crunchbase or Dealroom (paid stubs off).

indicators.name: Quarters from founding to $100M run-rate
indicators.unpublished_reason: Not measurable: seed/entities.yaml carries no founding dates, and the only run-rate series (Epoch, labs) dates a figure when the press reports it, not when the company crossed a hundred million.

indicators.name: Growth in tokens routed through a public router
indicators.unpublished_reason: Waiting on history: the router's snapshots start in September 2026, and a growth fit on a few days of a trailing-window total would be noise. It publishes once eight weeks of snapshots exist.
